title: Regional handback ladder for overload and error signals
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional overloads and transient downstream model errors we need a deterministic, graded mechanism to move traffic between region/tier/model-variant targets without triggering full blunt fallbacks that cause cascading cost/regression impact. Current circuit-breakers are binary and reactive; they either trip or not and lack graded cutovers, per-tenant sensitivity, and multi-signal smoothing (429 spikes + latency outliers + error-rate).

Goal: Design and implement a "handback ladder" — a stateful, signal-fused controller that steps traffic through a ladder of degradation actions (reduce tier allocation, shift small % to cheaper variant, increase KV-cache reuse, and finally escalate to regional fallback) with hysteresis, cooldown, and per-tenant/route sensitivity. The controller should support automatic triggers from 429s, timeouts, and error-rate thresholds, combine signals into a trip score, and expose telemetry and runbook hooks for operators.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New controller deployed behind feature-flag for a pilot tenant group.
2) Controller accepts multi-signal input (429-rate, p95 latency, timeout count, model-error-count) and produces stepwise traffic policies (tier-weight-adjust, model-variant-split, region-redirect) documented in the API.
3) Demonstrated smooth roll forward/back across simulated overload scenarios with no >3x spike in 5xxs for pilot tenants.
4) Observability: per-tenant trip-score, active ladder-step, cooldown remaining, and action audit trail visible in Console dashboard.
5) Automated unit+integration tests plus chaos simulation harness pass in CI.
6) Runbook and rollback plan published in Confluence and on-call runbook annotated.
plan:
Phase 1 (design + simulation, 2 wks): define trip-score math, ladder steps, hysteresis, per-tenant sensitivity; build a small Python simulation to validate parameters.
Phase 2 (impl, 3 wks): implement controller as a service in routing plane with a GRPC config API, integrate input signals from telemetry aggregator, and implement action engine to emit rate-limit and route-weight deltas.
Phase 3 (pilot + observability, 2 wks): pilot behind feature flag for 3 tenants in us-west/us-east, add Console panels and alerts, run chaos tests.
Phase 4 (rollout, 1 wk): expand to all hosted API traffic with conservative default thresholds and toggleable tenant sensitivity.

Engineering tasks:
- telemetry adapter: aggregate signals into per-tenant rolling windows (Miguel)
- trip-score service: implement scoring and hysteresis (Lina)
- action engine: translate steps into concrete routing adjustments (Omar)
- Console panels: telemetry + audit trail (Priya)
- Tests: simulation harness + integration tests (QA)

Feature-flag gating and metrics will be added to enable quick rollback.
decisions:
1) Use a weighted additive trip-score combining z-score of p95 latency, 429 per-1m rate, and model-error-rate with configurable weights per project.
2) Ladder steps will be staged: small regional split (5-15%), tier-trim (reduce dedicated pool weight), model-variant split (route to quantized/cheaper variant), cache-first preference, full regional cutover as last resort.
3) Hysteresis: require sustained score above threshold for 30s to step up, and require 3x longer sustained period below a lower threshold to step down (cooldown factor = 3).
4) Per-tenant sensitivity: customers can set "aggressiveness" low/medium/high; default medium.
5) Actions are advisory (emit policy deltas) and require route controller to commit them atomically with audit entries.
6) No automatic promotions to higher-risk variants without a manual opt-in per customer.
